negative_findings.description: No evidence found of a Fitch Ratings public rating on Tatra banka; search results indicated Fitch does not rate that issuer, and no 2025 Fitch action on Slovenská sporiteľňa surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fitch coverage of SK banks appears thinner than Moody's/S&P; Fitch is mainly a sovereign-rating source for SK.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids wasted collection effort building a Fitch-per-bank crawler; sets expectation that bank-level coverage is Moody's/S&P-centric.

negative_findings.description: ECB Supervisory Banking Statistics reports state there are no significant institutions at the highest level of consolidation in Slovakia, so SK banks are consolidated into their foreign parents (Erste, Intesa, RBI, KBC, UniCredit).
negative_findings.result_summary: SSM country tables give limited standalone SK bank-level detail.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: SK subsidiary-level analyst validation must come from EBA transparency data, NBS, registeruz filings and parent-group segment reporting rather than SSM aggregates.

negative_findings.description: Slovak-language queries for Big Four banking-sector studies returned mostly service/marketing pages and a Czech-language Deloitte press release, not SK-specific published banking surveys.
negative_findings.result_summary: Big Four SK-market banking research appears to be published regionally (CE/CEE) in English rather than as standalone Slovak-language studies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring of Big Four should focus on press rooms and short commentary; the substantive numbers arrive via CE/CEE English reports.

negative_findings.description: No Scope Ratings coverage of Slovak banks was surfaced by the searches performed; only S&P BICRA material was found for the country-risk angle.
negative_findings.result_summary: Scope's SK bank coverage unconfirmed — treat as unverified, not absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A smaller EU-registered agency could be a cheaper alternative source; needs a dedicated targeted check on scoperatings.com.

negative_findings.description: Substantive rating-agency credit opinions (Moody's, S&P) and most Big Four full reports sit behind subscriptions or registration forms; only headline ratings, rating-action press releases and regulatory disclosures are freely readable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Free layer = headline ratings + action releases; paid layer = the analytical detail.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Budget and licensing decisions are needed if the programme wants the restated asset-quality/capital detail this cell is meant to deliver.

brief: Analyst/auditor/agency coverage of Slovak banking splits into three tiers: a free notification layer (Moody's rating-news releases, S&P regulatory disclosures, issuer IR rating pages, MF SR and Slovak business press), a free analytical layer of institutional aggregators (IMF Article IV plus the unusually rich 2025 SVK FSAP technical notes, EBA EU-wide transparency bank-by-bank data, NBS Správa o finančnej stabilite, ECB SUP data), and a paid/gated layer holding the restated detail (full Moody's/S&P credit opinions, Deloitte Digital Banking Maturity and CEE Banking M&A study). Local-language coverage is genuinely productive on the statutory side — registeruz.sk carries the 'správa nezávislého audítora' with auditor identity and key audit matters for every SK bank — but Big Four SK research is published regionally in English rather than in Slovak. A structural caveat shapes everything here: Slovakia has no significant institution at the highest level of consolidation under the SSM, so subsidiary-level validation must come from EBA/NBS/registeruz and parent-group segment reporting rather than ECB aggregates. Main open gaps are parent-group analyst material, payments-sector analyst coverage, and confirmed Fitch/Scope entity-level coverage.
